verdict.rationale: The evidence pack has no AI-training policy or opt-out control for Cal.com's hosted service. The only route to keeping data out of vendor hands is self-hosting the MIT-licensed Cal.diy fork, which gives users full control over their scheduling infrastructure and needs no Cal.com account, but community reports say it is recommended for personal, non-production use and no longer ships public Docker images. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that customer data is not used for AI training, a user-facing training opt-out on the hosted product, and a self-hosted option endorsed for production.
